query_text: Set up a new router for wifi access

messages.content: Set up a new router for wifi access

message.content:
To set up a new router for **Wi‑Fi access**, connect it to your modem, power everything on in the right order, then use a browser or app to create your wireless network name and password.[1][3]

- Place the router in a **central, elevated, open** location, away from thick walls, metal objects, microwaves, cordless phones, and other sources of interference.[1][2]
- Unpack the router, attach any antennas, and connect an Ethernet cable from the modem’s **WAN/Internet** port to the router’s **WAN/Internet** port.[1][2][3]
- Power off the modem first, wait about 30 seconds, then power it back on and wait 2–3 minutes before turning on the router.[1][3]
- Connect your computer to the router with Ethernet if possible, or use the router’s default Wi‑Fi network name (SSID) from the label or documentation.[1][2]
- Open a web browser and go to the router’s setup address, which is often **192.168.1.1**, **192.168.0.1**, or the manufacturer’s setup page such as **tplinkwifi.net**.[1][3]
- Log in with the default credentials from the router label or manual, then change the **admin password** right away.[1][2][3]
- Follow the setup wizard to choose your internet connection type, then set your **Wi‑Fi name (SSID)** and **Wi‑Fi password**.[1][3]
- Save the settings and let the router test the connection.[3]
- After setup, update the **firmware** if available and review security settings such as disabling WPS if your router offers that option.[1][4]

If you want, I can also give you a **model-specific setup checklist** for your router brand, such as TP-Link, Netgear, ASUS, or Linksys.
